title: Compatibility verification: streaming + tool/function-calling for newly onboarded models
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Goal: Verify that newly onboarded models (both community and curated variants) are fully compatible with the platform's streaming API and the function/tool-calling flow. This ticket covers verification steps, automated test additions, manual edge-case checks, and publishing a compatibility result (pass/warn/fail) to the model catalog performance profile. We must ensure that streamed tokens, function call metadata, and mid-stream tool invocation behaviors are consistent across model variants and quantization profiles.

Background: Recent onboarding of two internal curated LLaMA-derivatives and an open-source instruction-tuned model exposed mismatches in streaming chunk sizes and in-flight function-call signaling. Some models emit special tokens mid-stream that the runtime previously treated as EOS; others delay JSON function payloads across token boundaries, breaking the function-calling SDK layers. We need a reproducible verification matrix so product and runtime teams can rely on the published compatibility flag in the model catalog.
acceptance_criteria: Automated compatibility test suite added to runtime-ci that runs against onboarding harness and passes for candidate models
For each model variant, catalog entry includes a streaming+tool-calling compatibility value (pass/warn/fail) and short notes
No regressions in existing streaming customers when compatibility flag is enabled (smoke tests green)
Handbook entry describing known failure modes and mitigation steps created in Confluence
tasks: Define test vectors: edge prompts that trigger function calls, long-stream tokenization, and mid-function JSON boundary cases
Implement harness extension in onboarding service to exercise streaming protocol and function-calling handshake
Add CI job (runtime-ci) that runs harness against candidate model container images and quantization variants
Add SDK e2e test that verifies function call metadata is preserved when streaming is used (node/python)
Instrument runtime to expose stream chunking and function-call events to observability (temporary tracing flag)
Run manual verification on curated models and document results in model catalog PR
If failures found, create follow-up ENG tickets for runtime fixes or model handler shims
comments: 2026-03-10 - Anika Patel: Created ticket after post-onboarding triage. Observed two failure classes: premature EOS on special tokens, and split JSON payloads across token boundaries for function metadata.
2026-03-11 - Jorge Morales: Implemented initial harness stub and uploaded prototype test vectors to Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/onboarding/stream-tool-harness (internal).
2026-03-11 - Priya Shah (QA): Reviewed vectors; suggested adding a long-running stream test that includes intermittent tool calls to simulate agent workflows.

2026-03-12 - Jorge Morales: Pushed PR with harness extension: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2148. Failing cases reproduced locally for open-llam-ft-13b-quant. Skipping quantized variants in CI until we add model shims.
2026-03-12 - Marco Li (Product): Requested that catalog compatibility flags surface a "probable-warning" state for quantized variants pending further investigation.
notes: Trade-offs considered: adding conservative buffering in the runtime to reassemble fragmented function-call JSON solves many model-level issues but increases tail latency. Decided to first detect and flag models as WARN/FAIL in the catalog and only apply buffering via opt-in compatibility shims for Dedicated customers with SLA requirements. Long-term plan is avoiding buffering by improving tokenizers/handlers in model packaging guide.
qa_plan: 1) Run CI job against current candidate images and verify status. 2) Run SDK e2e with simulated agent that performs 10k tool calls across short/long streams. 3) Execute chaos-injection test to drop middle stream packets and validate graceful recovery. 4) Publish findings and mark model catalog entry with compatibility flag.
next_steps: Merge PR 2148 and enable runtime tracing for two hours in staging to gather chunking telemetry
Add the compatibility result publishing step to onboarding pipeline
Schedule 30-min sync with Model Onboarding PM and Console owner to map UI flag surface
